name: Asemic Hand
desc: An invisible scribe writes invented cursive script -- stroke by stroke, line by line -- down a toned parchment page: a flowing nonsense hand with ascenders, descenders and loops, nib-pressure weight and ink pooling where the pen dwells, a soft raking light travelling across the sheet as it fills; when the page is finished it is set aside and a fresh sheet in a new hand begins, a perpetual scriptorium that never settles. Rendered in sepia iron-gall, indigo, charcoal, or as chalk on a blueprint negative.

energy.doc: ink darkness, stroke contrast and raking-light glow

scale.doc: size of the writing -- larger hand, fewer words per line (obvious change)

speed.doc: how fast the pen writes and how often the page turns

density.doc: lines per page / tightness of the script

hue.doc: paper + ink tone for the sepia default; other styles fix their own

style.doc: aesthetic: warm iron-gall on parchment / indigo ink / grey charcoal / chalk on a blueprint negative

seed.doc: deterministic -- re-throws the hand, the words, the page toning
